scope.summary: Prove, at runtime, that Handshake can launch a model lane against a worktree-scoped folder running inside a microVM - the second half of the Operator's non-negotiable. The first half (an operator-selected FOLDER really becoming the spawned child's working directory) is already proven by operator_chat_cli_lane_runs_in_operator_selected_cwd, which drives SpawnRequest.working_dir -> CliBridgeConfig.working_dir -> the real child process cwd, with a negative control showing the child does NOT land there when working_dir is absent. This MT covers the VM half, which currently has no live proof.

acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A model lane launches against a worktree-scoped folder inside a microVM and produces REAL generated tokens from a model loaded inside that VM. Fake adapters and in-memory doubles do not satisfy this; per HBR-STOP-003 and the Spec-Realism Gate the proof must touch the real managed resource boundary.

AC-2: The worktree_id -> VM binding is durable and recoverable: after a restart the binding resolves to the same VM (or fails closed with a named reason), proven against real PostgreSQL rather than in-memory state.

AC-3: Process ownership holds across the VM boundary (HBR-QUIET-003): the VM-hosted lane records START/STOP with owner metadata and is reclaimed on session close, failure, staleness, or operator cancel, leaving no orphan VM.

AC-4: HBR-PRIV: the worktree-VM binding and any artifact it produces carry owner_account_id / actor_principal_id / workspace scope per the account-bound resource scope introduced in migrations 0363+0364 and swarm_orchestration/resource_scope.rs, with a cross-account negative proving one account cannot enumerate or attach to another account's worktree VM.

AC-5: The in-product internal UserManual documents the worktree-VM launch path (purpose, usage, inputs/outputs, failure modes, recovery) and records the HBR-INT-009 three-tier diagnostic posture, with internal_diagnostics/Palmistry marked DEFERRED-with-reason while WP-KERNEL-012 is unshipped.

A VM that outlives its session is an orphan with far higher cost than an orphan process; AC-3 is not optional.
Marking this MT NOT_APPLICABLE because 'WP-KERNEL-004 owns the VM' would lose the Operator's non-negotiable. The seam is KERNEL-004's; proving the model-launch lane over it is this packet's.

research_basis_2026_08_05.operator_request: Handshake should have a BUILT-IN hypervisor/KVM capability; operator prefers Rust or an open-source Docker variant in Rust.
research_basis_2026_08_05.terminology_correction: A program cannot 'contain' /dev/kvm - it is a Linux kernel device node exposed by the kvm module, not something an application provides. The achievable form of the request is: Handshake BUNDLES AND MANAGES its own Rust virtualization backend, so the operator installs nothing. On Linux/WSL2 that backend talks to /dev/kvm; on native Windows the equivalent hardware interface is WHP (Windows Hypervisor Platform).
research_basis_2026_08_05.existing_precedent_in_this_codebase: handshake_core already implements exactly this pattern for a different dependency: managed_postgres.rs starts, owns, and tears down its own PostgreSQL with an explicit data dir and port. A managed hypervisor is the same shape, which is why 'built-in' is architecturally cheap here rather than novel.

candidates_evaluated.cloud-hypervisor: Rust, Apache-2.0, production-grade, KVM/Linux only. ALREADY integrated as sandbox/cloud_hypervisor with a persistent-VM + snapshot/restore seam and WorktreeVmRegistry. Cheapest path to a working proof because the adapter code already exists; needs the binary provisioned. Does NOT run natively on Windows.
candidates_evaluated.OpenVMM (microsoft/openvmm, MIT): Rust, cross-platform VMM: Windows x64/Aarch64 via WHP, Linux via KVM or MSHV, macOS via Hypervisor.framework. The only evaluated option that gives a FULL VM natively on Windows with no WSL2. Microsoft states it is not yet production-ready.
candidates_evaluated.Hyperlight (Microsoft -> CNCF Sandbox): Rust EMBEDDABLE micro-VM library; hardware isolation via KVM, MSHV, or WHP; sub-millisecond starts. Best fit for 'built-in' since it is a library, not a daemon. CAVEAT recorded honestly: it targets small functions/Wasm workloads; running a full local LLM inside one is not its design point today (Hyperlight Nanvix is adding POSIX support but is early). Not a drop-in for AC-1 as written.
candidates_evaluated.youki / libcontainer-rs: Rust OCI runtime, memory-safe runc replacement, containerd-validated, ~30% faster start. Linux-only by nature (namespaces/cgroups). The right choice for the CONTAINER lane, not the VM lane.
candidates_evaluated.ocipkg / ocirender: Rust OCI registry client and image assembly without a daemon - the 'docker pull' half if a container lane is built.
candidates_evaluated.REJECTED - 'full-feature Docker in Rust': Does not exist. youki (runtime), ocipkg/ocirender (images) and netavark/aardvark (networking) are real and production-grade, but no project assembles them into a Docker-equivalent engine. Recorded as rejected so nobody re-searches for it expecting to find one.

runtime_capability_proof_2026_08_05.headline: The microVM sandbox WORKS on this host, proven at runtime. Every component the 2026-08-04 BLOCKED record called missing is present and functional.
runtime_capability_proof_2026_08_05.what_was_actually_run: cloud-hypervisor --kernel vmlinux-6.1.102 --initramfs initramfs.cpio --cmdline 'console=ttyS0 hsk.cmd=<base64>' --cpus boot=2 --memory size=1024M --serial tty --console off
runtime_capability_proof_2026_08_05.observed_output: Run /init as init process / ---HSK-BEGIN--- / Linux (none) 6.1.102 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC x86_64 GNU/Linux / GUEST_CPUS=2 / ISOLATION_HOSTFS=0 / ---HSK-END rc=0--- / ACPI: PM: Preparing to enter system sleep state S5 / reboot: Power down
what_this_proves: A real Linux 6.1.102 kernel boots under cloud-hypervisor (a Rust VMM) on this host's KVM.
Arbitrary commands execute INSIDE the guest and their output returns to the host through the serial transport, with a typed begin/end/rc envelope the init contract defines.
The vCPU count honours the host-side --cpus flag (GUEST_CPUS=2), so guest resources are really being shaped by the caller.
ISOLATION_HOSTFS=0: the guest sees NOTHING of the host filesystem. This is real isolation, not a chroot-shaped claim.
Clean lifecycle: rc=0 then ACPI S5 power down, so the VM terminates rather than leaking.

portability_defect_FIXED_2026_08_05.was: Five compile-time constants hardcoded one operator's home directory: DEFAULT_WORK_DIR, DEFAULT_CH_BIN, DEFAULT_CH_REMOTE_BIN, DEFAULT_KERNEL and DEFAULT_INITRAMFS all began '/home/ilja_smets/handshake-sandbox'. They sat directly beneath a doc comment claiming the adapter 'stays disk-agnostic per [GLOBAL-PORTABILITY] (no hardcoded absolute path is baked into a build the operator cannot redirect after a project move)' - the comment and the code contradicted each other.
portability_defect_FIXED_2026_08_05.now: A runtime resolver replaces them. default_sandbox_root() resolves in order: HANDSHAKE_SANDBOX_ROOT, then $HOME (or $USERPROFILE on Windows) joined with 'handshake-sandbox', then a bare relative directory as last resort. default_work_dir/default_ch_bin/default_ch_remote_bin/default_kernel/default_initramfs derive from it. The existing HANDSHAKE_CH_* overrides are unchanged and still win, so no operator-facing behaviour changed on a configured host.
portability_defect_FIXED_2026_08_05.why_it_mattered_beyond_the_rule: This is also what made the installed binaries invisible to a PATH-based probe and produced the FALSE 'cloud-hypervisor ABSENT' blocker recorded on 2026-08-04: the adapter resolved absolute paths while the probe searched PATH.
